verdicts.reason: A: clean left-to-right order with readable one-line subcopy, but the CTA hangs half off the dark text panel's right edge and the logo floats awkwardly above the panel. B: the 'Solstice' headline nearly touches the CTA button with no gutter, and the subcopy wraps to leave an orphaned 'longest day.' line.

A: balanced banner with readable one-line subcopy and clear headline/CTA hierarchy, though the can is shrunk to a small icon and hugs the left edge. B: the subcopy is shrunk to illegible fine print in the bottom-left, far from its headline, and the headline runs right up against the CTA.

A: the subcopy is microscopic and unreadable, the Solstice logo is moved down to a tiny mark beside it at the bottom (logo trivialised), and the headline collides with the CTA. B: clean layout with readable subcopy and proper hierarchy; the only flaw is a can that is undersized and pushed to the left edge.

A: reversed reading order, with the CTA placed first on the left before the headline and jammed against 'Sip'; the subcopy wraps to an orphaned 'longest day.'; the can is pushed to the right edge. B: order and hierarchy are fine, but the subcopy is shrunk to illegible fine print in the bottom-left corner, detached from the headline, which breaks readability.
